title: Salesforce Developer
description: From the data model to PD II: SOQL, Flows, Apex, triggers, limits, async and LWC, practised on real problems graded in your org.

nodes.title: Data model
nodes.summary: Objects, fields, relationships and how records connect.
nodes.lesson:
Everything in Salesforce is a **record** of an **object** (Account, Contact, Opportunity, or your own `Thing__c`). Objects have **fields**; custom ones end in `__c`.

Relationships link objects:

- **Lookup**: a loose link (a Contact *looks up* to an Account). Deleting the parent doesn't delete the child.
- **Master-detail**: a tight link. The child inherits sharing and is deleted with the parent; the parent can have **roll-up summary** fields.

You'll query these relationships in SOQL next: child-to-parent with dots (`Account.Name`), parent-to-child with subqueries (`(SELECT Id FROM Contacts)`).

nodes.title: Triggers
nodes.lesson:
A **trigger** is Apex that runs when records are inserted, updated, deleted or undeleted. It receives the records in **context variables**: `Trigger.new` (the new versions), `Trigger.old` (the previous ones, on update and delete), and the `Trigger.newMap` / `Trigger.oldMap` versions keyed by Id.

**Before** triggers run before the record is saved: change fields on `Trigger.new` directly and Salesforce saves them, with no DML. **After** triggers run once the record has an Id: use them to create or update *other* records.

Triggers fire for up to **200 records at a time**, so every trigger must be **bulk-safe**: no queries or DML inside loops. Collect what you need into sets and maps, query once, then loop.

Where triggers sit among everything else that happens on save is called the **order of execution**:
nodes.diagramCaption: Order of execution, simplified: before-save flows, before triggers, validation and duplicate rules, the save, after triggers, assignment rules, after-save flows, roll-ups, then commit and post-commit work.
concepts: The difference between `Trigger.new`, `Trigger.old`, `Trigger.newMap` and `Trigger.oldMap`, and when each is null
Same-record field changes go in **before** triggers; changes to other records go in **after** triggers
Bulkification: one query and one DML statement per trigger run, whatever the batch size
One trigger per object, delegating to a handler class
How to stop recursion when an after trigger updates records that fire it again
pitfalls: Running `update` on `Trigger.new` in a before trigger: it fails. Assign the fields and let the save do it.
A SOQL query inside the loop: fine for one record in testing, a `LimitException` at 101 records.
Using `Trigger.old` in an insert trigger: it's null there.
Several triggers on one object: their order isn't guaranteed, so behaviour changes between deploys.

resources.title: Trigger and bulk request best practices

quiz.q: Look at the diagram. A before-save flow and a before trigger both set the same field. Whose value is saved?
quiz.imageAlt: The order of execution: before-save flows run first, then before triggers, then validation rules.
quiz.why: Before-save flows run first (step 1) and before triggers run after them (step 2), so the trigger's assignment is the one that's saved.

quiz.q: Using the diagram: a validation rule fails. Has the after trigger run?
quiz.imageAlt: The order of execution: validation rules are step 3, after triggers are step 6.
options: No: validation fails before the save, and after triggers come after it
Only if the trigger is active
quiz.why: Validation runs before the record is saved (step 3). A failure stops the save, so steps 5 onwards, including after triggers, never run.

quiz.q: Where should you set a field on the same record that's being inserted?
options: After insert trigger with an update statement
Before insert trigger, assigning on Trigger.new
quiz.why: Before triggers can change Trigger.new directly; the save writes the change with no extra DML.

quiz.q: Which context variable is null in an insert trigger?
quiz.why: There's no previous version of a record being inserted, so Trigger.old and Trigger.oldMap are null.

nodes.title: Apex testing
nodes.summary: Test classes, test data, asserts and 75% coverage.
nodes.lesson:
Every SFCode problem is graded by a hidden **test class**, the same way Salesforce gates production deploys.

- Mark classes `@IsTest`; methods `@IsTest static void ...`.
- Create your own data in the test. Never rely on org data (`SeeAllData=true`).
- Wrap the action in `Test.startTest()` / `Test.stopTest()`: you get fresh governor limits, and async work runs at `stopTest`.
- Assert outcomes with `Assert.areEqual(expected, actual, message)`.
- Production deploys need **75%** coverage overall and every trigger covered.

Test **bulk**: insert 200 records, not 1.
